PMID:42367434.topic: Non-hip femoral fragility fracture surgery timing and weight bearing
PMID:42367434.setting: Seven NHS hospitals in the Wessex Deanery (Southampton, Portsmouth, Poole, Salisbury, Basingstoke, Dorchester, Isle of Wight); multicentre retrospective audit
PMID:42367434.standard: BOAST 'The care of the older or frail orthopaedic trauma patient' (2019) point 14: all surgery in the frail patient should allow full weight bearing and be performed within 36 hours of admission

cycle1.result: Of 342 patients with time-to-surgery data, 86 (25%) had surgery within 36 hours; 256 had surgery after 36 hours. FWB prescribed in 41 (76%) arthroplasty vs 173 (57%) fixation patients; arthroplasty patients breached 36 hours more often (n = 46, 85%) than fixation (n = 218, 72%).

PMID:42367434.other_findings: Fixation (n = 303, 85%) was the main treatment; FWB was achieved by 36 (87%) arthroplasty vs 121 (70%) fixation patients prescribed it. Median length of stay was 13 days with surgery within 36 hours vs 17 days after, and NWB patients were less often discharged home (21% vs 56% FWB).

PMID:38024031.setting: St Richard's Hospital, Chichester; district general hospital trauma and orthopaedic department
PMID:38024031.standard: GMC Decision Making and Consent (2020), RCS England Consent: Supported Decision-Making (2016) and the BOA-endorsed orthoconsent.com model hip fracture consent form

cycle1.result: Infection documented in 98.4%, blood clots 95.2%, bleeding 92.1%, neurovascular injury 79.4%, dislocation 77.8%, pain 74.6%, anaesthetic complications 73%, failure 68.3%, leg length discrepancy 60.3%, bone damage/fracture 50.8%, death 49.2%, wound complications 42.9%, hip stiffness 14.3%, catheterisation 0%. Diagnosis missing in 22.2% (n=14), benefits in 12.7% (n=8), responsible consultant in 28.6% (n=18), blood transfusion in 25.4% (n=16).

PMID:38024031.other_findings: 52.4% of consents were taken by SHOs/core trainees without formal orthopaedic training; orthopaedic-specific risks were documented less often than generic risks (p<0.00001). Patient name and date were missing beside the signature in 57.1% (n=36); induction teaching, governance presentation and posting the model form were recommended with a planned re-audit.

PMID:34048561.setting: Kamsar Hospital, Boké region, Western Guinea; referral hospital neonatal and general paediatric units

cycle1.result: 39 of 5670 admissions (0.7%) were tetanus (22 NNT, 17 PNNT); 21 (53.8%) died within 7 days (NNT 16/22, 72.7%; PNNT 5/17, 29.4%).

PMID:34048561.other_findings: 36/39 (92.3%) were born to unvaccinated or suboptimally vaccinated mothers; severe disease was the only factor linked with mortality after adjustment. Cases at the hospital were not reflected in WHO national reports, suggesting under-reporting.

PMID:31468111.topic: Preoperative epoetin for anaemia in hip arthroplasty
PMID:31468111.setting: Polyclinique de la Thiérache, Wignehies; single-surgeon series of primary total hip arthroplasty

cycle1.result: Group A (anaesthetist-prescribed EPO, 4 weekly 40,000 IU for Hb 10–13 g/dl): EPO given to 43 (6.7%); mean total dose 115,349 IU; bleeding index 2.7 ± 1.0; 5 (0.8%) transfused up to POD7.

PMID:31468111.intervention: Amended EPO protocol (2013) prescribed by the surgeon: two injections of 20,000–40,000 IU at 14 and 7 days before surgery for Hb <12 g/dl in patients at high transfusion risk.

cycle2.result: Group S: EPO given to 26 (3.4%) (p = 0.006); mean total dose 75,200 IU (p < 0.001); bleeding index 2.8 ± 1.0 (p = 0.375); 0 transfused up to POD7 (p = 0.021).

PMID:31468111.other_findings: No patient who received EPO was transfused, and EPO-treated patients had a lower bleeding index (2.2 ± 1.0 vs 2.8 ± 1.0, p < 0.001). In 2017 the protocol was changed again to Hb <11.5 g/dl and 20,000 IU doses.

PMID:32951919.topic: Virtual fracture clinic referral and remote follow-up
PMID:32951919.setting: Great Western Hospital, Swindon; 480-bed district general hospital fracture clinic and virtual fracture clinic during COVID-19
PMID:32951919.standard: BOAST COVID-19 guidance points 7–10: removable casts/splints in 100%; index fracture clinic appointments 100% virtually screened; follow-up by phone/video in 100%; follow-up radiographs for union in 0% (exceptions if documented)

cycle1.result: 100% removable casts; 96% virtually assessed or approved for face-to-face (197 VFC, 18 approved, 8 no approval); 97% virtual follow-up or documented reason (6/223, 2.7% without); 0.4% inappropriate radiographs for union.

PMID:32951919.intervention: All patients required a consultant-level senior opinion (trauma meeting, on-call consultant or VFC) before a face-to-face appointment, from 11 May 2020; email reminder to use virtual clinics.

cycle2.result: 100% removable casts; 99% virtually assessed or consultant-approved (130 VFC, 14 approved, 1 unapproved); 100% virtual follow-up or documented reason; 0.7% inappropriate radiographs for union.

PMID:32951919.other_findings: A simulated virtual clinic for the 26 patients first seen face to face showed 22 appointments and 13 X-ray attendances could have been saved. The one unapproved re-audit patient was a GP referral, so GP and outside referrals are now discussed with the VFC team.

PMID:36570114.topic: Suspected cauda equina time to MRI
PMID:36570114.setting: Poole Hospital (University Hospitals Dorset); district general hospital emergency department and orthopaedics

cycle1.result: Mean MRI completion from arrival 13:54:49; mean MRI request from arrival 14:12:03; arrival to action plan 27:29:00; 28% stayed less than 24 hours.

PMID:36570114.intervention: Findings shared with ED and radiology; reserved MRI slots for suspected CES booked directly by ED with prioritised vetting; red-flag checklist and bladder scan protocol; proposed CES pathway; posters and pathway distributed to ED and orthopaedic staff.

cycle2.result: Mean MRI completion from arrival 10:39:00; mean MRI request from arrival 06:10:00; arrival to action plan 15:38 (43.1% reduction vs cycle 1); 54.4% stayed less than 24 hours.

PMID:36570114.other_findings: Three cycles; the second (1 June–16 July 2021, n=50) showed MRI completion 12:24:00, MRI delay from order 5:01:32 and 36% staying under 24 hours. Mean inpatient stay rose in cycle 3 (85:08:00) due to complex discharges; 8/168 (4.7%) had CES.

PMID:41664711.setting: Orthopaedic Department, James Paget University Hospital, Gorleston; enhanced recovery pathway for primary TKR
PMID:41664711.standard: Mobilisation within 24 hours after surgery, in keeping with ERAS principles and local pathway expectations

cycle1.result: 35/53 (66.0%) mobilised within 24 hours; median length of stay 2 days.

PMID:41664711.intervention: MAKE1 findings presented to the multidisciplinary team; reinforcement of enhanced recovery practices, better documentation of reasons for delayed mobilisation and prompt management/escalation of pain, nausea and hypotension.

cycle2.result: 57/63 (90.5%) mobilised within 24 hours; median length of stay 2 days.

PMID:41664711.other_findings: Pain remained the commonest barrier and was linked to longer stay (mean 5.2 days in MAKE2). No POD 0 physiotherapy assessments were documented, and no clear difference was seen between spinal and general anaesthesia.

PMID:32547634.setting: Royal Gwent Hospital, Newport; 774-bed district general hospital trauma and orthopaedics
PMID:32547634.standard: Royal College of Surgeons consent standards

cycle1.result: Procedure details documented 93%; abbreviations used in 38%; procedure-specific risks documented 31%; copy offered to patient 12%.

PMID:32547634.intervention: Cycle 1 (January 2018): induction and departmental teaching on consent plus senior review of consent forms on the morning ward round. Cycle 2 (August 2018): hip fracture proforma with pre-printed procedure-specific consent risk stickers and induction teaching on their use.

cycle2.result: Procedure details documented 100%; abbreviations 7%; procedure-specific risks documented 67%; copy offered to patient 8%.

PMID:32547634.other_findings: After teaching alone (January 2018, n=26) abbreviations fell to 20%, procedure-specific risks rose to 72% and copies offered to 48%. Sticker supplies ran out and formal use fell below 75% of forms, and offering a copy fell once it was not prompted.

PMID:38752056.topic: Native hip dislocation time to reduction
PMID:38752056.setting: Major trauma centre, University Hospital of Wales, Cardiff; plus survey of Welsh EDs and UK MTCs
PMID:38752056.standard: No formal standard; practice measured against reduction within 6 hours and 12 hours of injury, based on published research

cycle1.result: Mean time to reduction 532 minutes (240–804); 4 (29%) reduced within 6 hours and 11 (79%) within 12 hours (abstract gives 28.6% and 71.4%). ED reductions (n=2) mean 275 minutes vs theatre (n=13) 576 minutes.

PMID:38752056.other_findings: Post-reduction neurovascular status documented in 100% and post-reduction CT in 87%; one AVN and one chondrolysis. Most Welsh EDs (20% with pathway) and UK MTCs (23% with pathway) lacked a pathway; a native hip dislocation ED pathway was introduced in February 2023 but not re-audited.

PMID:19442310.topic: Foot care provision in rheumatoid arthritis
PMID:19442310.setting: Rheumatology outpatient clinics, Counties Manukau District Health Board, Auckland
PMID:19442310.standard: Arthritis and Musculoskeletal Alliance (ARMA) Standards of Care for People with Foot Health Problems and Inflammatory Arthritis

cycle1.result: 77% reported no previous formal foot assessment; 76% had not seen a podiatrist; 40% had used the orthotic centre; 27% had previous foot surgery; over 85% had foot lesions.

PMID:19442310.other_findings: No patient had seen a podiatrist specialising in rheumatic disease, as the service only covered diabetes; many wore inappropriate open footwear (sandals 21%, mules 13%, jandals 10%). A specialist podiatrist within the rheumatology team was recommended.

PMID:32190793.setting: Bristol Royal Hospital for Children; tertiary paediatric hospital (paediatric medicine, surgery and orthopaedics)
PMID:32190793.standard: 17 admission documentation standards based on Royal College of Physicians clerking standards and RCPCH/PRSB digital record standards; aim to raise average compliance from 59% to above 90%

cycle1.result: Blank continuation sheets: 5 of 17 standards >90%, none 100%; medications 48%, allergies 47%, social history 36%, responsible consultant 8%, accompanying adult 24%, observations 38%.

PMID:32190793.intervention: Specialty-specific colour-coded pre-printed admission booklets with prompts and tick boxes (medicine, surgery, orthopaedics), introduced March 2019 with teaching at junior doctor handovers.

cycle2.dates: From March 2019 (first 40 booklet admissions per specialty)
cycle2.result: Average 33% absolute improvement (P < 0.01); 12 of 17 standards >90% and 4 at 100%; medications 99%, allergies 93%, consultant 88%, accompanying adult 68%, observations 52%.

PMID:32190793.other_findings: Observations (52%) and investigations (70%) remained poorly documented. Examination findings and plans were already well documented and changed little.

PMID:28567160.topic: Hip fracture orthogeriatric and preoperative medical assessment
PMID:28567160.setting: Chelsea & Westminster NHS Foundation Trust, London; district general hospital
PMID:28567160.standard: Cycle 1: Best Practice Tariff time to orthogeriatric assessment <72 hours and time to surgery <36 hours. Cycle 2: 100% preoperative medical assessment, orthogeriatric assessment <24 hours, time to surgery <36 hours

cycle1.result: Preoperative medical assessment 19%; mean time to orthogeriatric assessment 91 hours; mean time to surgery 37 hours; mean length of stay 24.8 days; inpatient mortality 14%.

PMID:28567160.intervention: New multidisciplinary hip fracture pathway from 1 June 2011: direct admission to the acute medical ward under joint named medical and orthopaedic consultants, anaesthetic assessment within 12 hours, consultant orthopaedic and orthogeriatric review within 24 hours; seminars and laminated posters for staff.

cycle2.result: Preoperative medical assessment 85% (p=0.0001); mean time to orthogeriatric assessment 19 hours (p=0.0001); mean time to surgery 31 hours (p=0.0663); length of stay 19.5 days (p=0.029); mortality 4% (p=0.0336).

PMID:28567160.other_findings: Return to original accommodation rose from 57% to 80% (p=0.0069), and delays over 36 hours due to inadequate medical optimisation fell from 41% to 17%. The main remaining cause of breaches was lack of morning trauma lists, since rescheduled.
